'''''Saponaria ocymoides''''', the '''rock soapwort'''<ref name=GRIN>{{GRIN | accessdate = 21 January 2018}}</ref> or '''tumbling Ted''',<ref name=GRIN/> is a [[species]] of semi-[[evergreen]] [[perennial plant|perennial]] [[flowering plant]] belonging to the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Caryophyllaceae]], [[native plant|native]] to south western and southern central Europe.<ref name=RHSAZ>{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1405332965|pages=1136}}</ref>

==Etymology==
The Latin [[binomial nomenclature|specific epithet]] ''ocymoides'' means “resembling basil” (''[[Ocimum]]'').<ref name=RHSLG>{{cite book | last=Harrison |first=Lorraine | title=RHS Latin for Gardeners | year=2012 |publisher=Mitchell Beazley | location=United Kingdom | isbn=978-1845337315 }}</ref> However the resemblance is superficial, as the two plants are not closely related. In fact ''Saponaria ocymoides'' belongs to the same family as pinks and carnations.

==Description==
Reaching a height of {{convert|10|-|40|cm}}, the stem is prostrate to ascending, woody, reddish, quite hairy and very branched. The leaves are ovate to lanceolate, sessile and hairy, 1–3 cm long. The five-petalled flowers are arranged in groups at the ends of branches.  They have red or pink (rarely white) [[petal]]s and blue [[anther]]s. The sepals are  fused in a tube about an 8 to 10 millimeters long. The flowering period extends from May to August in the Northern Hemisphere. The fruit is an ovoid capsule, up to 9 mm long.

==Distribution==
This species ranges from the mountains of Spain to Corsica, Sardinia and Slovenia, from the Apennines to the Alps. It grows in rocky and stony places, dry slopes and forests (especially pine forests). It prefers calcareous ([[alkali soil|alkaline]]) soils, at an elevation of up to {{convert|1500|m}}, rarely up to {{convert|2400|m}}.

==Cultivation==
''Saponaria ocymoides'' is cultivated as an ornamental plant for [[rock garden]]s and dry stone walls, in well-drained alkaline or neutral soil in full sun. Like most alpine plants it dislikes winter wetness around its roots.<ref name=RHSAZ /> It has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Saponaria ocymoides''|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/16440/Saponaria-ocymoides/Details | accessdate=19 February 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 
| page = 94 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | accessdate = 29 October 2018}}</ref>
